paper.title_en: On the large N convergence of the supermembrane matrix model
paper.abstract_en: In this paper, the large N behavior of a supersymmetric matrix model is compared with its exact continuum description. We prove that the complete spectrum of a $SU(N)$ regularized compactified M2-brane theory in the semiclassical approximation converges, in the large $N$ limit, to the exact spectrum in the same approximation. To this end, we concentrate on the large $N$ limit of a supersymmetric matrix model describing a supermembrane with central charge on a toroidally compactified target space. We analyze, on the one hand, the supermembrane model formulated on a differentiable compact torus, with structure group given by the area-preserving diffeomorphisms, and, on the other hand, its associated regularized $SU(N)$ model. We emphasize in our analysis the structure of the local and global constraints of the regularized model, which generate the $SU(N)$ algebra and reproduce the area-preserving diffeomorphism algebra in the large N limit, together with the topological information associated with the central charge condition and the topology of the model. We explain the role of the central charge in the compactified supermembrane and how it allows a top-down $SU(N)$ regularization. It is known that its $SU(N)$ regularized model has a purely discrete spectrum with finite multiplicity. We prove that, in the semiclassical approximation, the spectrum of the Hamiltonian of the supersymmetric matrix model converges in the large-$N$ limit to that of the Hamiltonian of the supermembrane (M2-brane) with central charge.
